A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original transformer experiments, including vision classification, BERT/GPT-2 evaluations, ablations, transfer tests, and LLaMA/CLIP analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The shared-classifier aligned loss, linearly increasing layer weights, alternating training procedure, and confidence-based early exits remain unchanged (Section 3 and Appendix B.3).

E1.justification: The same vision, GLUE, WikiText-103, detection, LLaMA, and CLIP evaluations remain, including the MNIST and transfer experiments. RTE/QQP results referenced more explicitly in v3 were already present in v2 Figure 21.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same standard-training, multi-exit/classifiers, cosine-regularized training, and BERT/GPT-2 comparators. No evaluated comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: Appendix C.1 and Figure 19 revise the reported LLaMA3.2 3B depth from 24 to 28 layers. v2 already specifies 28 layers in its Figure 20 discussion, and the plots are unchanged, supporting a configuration-reporting correction without evidence of rerunning experiments. Other settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The residual-connection controls, cosine-regularization and layer-weight ablations, neural-collapse analysis, transfer tests, and LLaMA/CLIP analyses are retained with the same evidence in Appendices B–D.

E5.justification: The sample-distribution box plots in Figures 10–11 are unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All plotted graphics and Table 1 values are unchanged. Section 3.1 retains 77.96% accuracy with 1.36× speedup for aligned training and 78.32% with 1.42× speedup for multi-exit/classifiers. The LLaMA depth correction concerns configuration reporting.

T1.justification: The assumptions, theorem statements, effective-depth definition, and Appendix A proofs are unchanged. Theorems 1–2 become 2.1–2.2 and Definition 1 becomes 3.1; replacing Tr with trace is equivalent notation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about cosine similarity, saturation events, improved shallow-layer performance, and single-classifier multi-exit models, including the novelty claim.

C2.justification: Both retain the approximate-geodesic caveat, equal-feature-dimension applicability boundary, and explanations concerning regularization, transferability, and the CLIP modality gap. No substantive interpretation or limitation is added.

D1.justification: The LLaMA3.2 3B configuration documentation becomes internally consistent through the 24-to-28-layer correction in Appendix C.1 and Figure 19. Optimizers, training schedules, hardware, generation settings, and dataset-access statements otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are retained. Numbered citations replace author–year citations, and reference ordering changes, without adding or removing prior work.

P1.justification: v3 updates the author/affiliation block, identifies the corresponding author, changes citation and theorem numbering conventions, copyedits captions, and adds figure pointers in Appendices B.1 and C.2. The narrative and section organization remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: A document-wide template change revises margins, typography, title layout, table presentation, and figure sizing and placement. Figures 3 and 7 become standalone centered figures instead of text-wrapped figures, and appendix displays are extensively repositioned. The underlying graphical content is retained.

improvement.justification: Correcting the LLaMA depth in Appendix C.1 and Figure 19 resolves an internal inconsistency with the existing 28-layer case study and plots. Small wording fixes and figure pointers also improve clarity. These are limited gains: the extensive reformatting leaves the method, proofs, empirical evidence, and conclusions unchanged.
